answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by grouping agents into small cohorts that share liability for each other's conduct. When one member cheats, every cohort member loses standing, so an attacker who floods a reef of traders with copies faces multiplied losses across all of them, like a lantern revealing each copy in turn. A canyon of past conduct separates trusted groups from fresh ones, and buying many copies never dilutes the risk, it multiplies it, so each extra fake identity raises the attacker's own exposure instead of buying extra votes.
